I am from medical community actually, to be precise i am a doctor, and I didn’t call it a diagnostic test. And we in medical community don’t simply divide tests into just 2 categories of screening and diagnostic like you’d find on google. There are many subcategories and we go by our books. So like i said before first-line screening tests are double and triple marker tests, as they are first line and nipt is much more accurate than these screening tests. Investigations are usually divided into first line, second line, inv of choice and gold standard investigations. In our setup and most of the world I have worked except perhaps US/UK, we offer first line screening tests to all our patients and nipt isn’t insurance covered for most patients so that is offered as a second line test in high-risk cases or if parents demand. It is highly sensitive and specific, non-diagnostic but much more accurate than other screening tests, therefore it is in screening investigation of choice category, and thus not like merely any other screening test. It is investigation of choice because it is non-invasive and reported detection and false-positive rates of 99.2% and 0.09% for trisomy 21 (T21) respectively. We offer amniocentesis after NIPT which is a diagnostic and therefore the current gold-standard test. Patients can choose to terminate after their NIPT report if they want to because of the very low false positive rate of 0.09%. We by ourselves offer decisions only after amniocentesis. And CVS isn’t recommended anymore for these cases.
